+## Pulumi
+
+The `pulumi` module shows the currently selected [Pulumi Stack](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/intro/concepts/stack/) and version.
+
+::: tip
+
+By default the Pulumi version is not shown, since it takes an order of magnitude longer to load then most plugins (~70ms).
+If you still want to enable it, [follow the example shown below](#with-pulumi-version).
+
+:::
+
+By default the module will be shown if any of the following conditions are met:
+
+- The current directory contains either `Pulumi.yaml` or `Pulumi.yml`
+- A parent directory contains either `Pulumi.yaml` or `Pulumi.yml`
+
+### Options
+
+| Option              | Default                              | Description                                                               |
+| ------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `format`            | `"via [$symbol$stack]($style) "`     | The format string for the module.                                         |
+| `version_format`    | `"v${raw}"`                          | The version format. Available vars are `raw`, `major`, `minor`, & `patch` |
+| `symbol`            | `"🚀 "`                                | A format string shown before the Pulumi stack.                          |

body: We will also need a description for the module here. It would be near line 211 of this file, but the web interface won't let me actually mark that line, so the comment is going here :(
Just want to say in advance: I'm not at all familiar with pulumi, so forgive me if some of these questions are naive.

While elegant in a functional sense, this takes a while to unpack and understand. Is there a reason we can't just increment a counter until we see three `'.'` characters (or hit the end of string) and then slice up to that index?
Not necessarily a blocker (we can add another PR afterwards if it would slow this down too much), but this feels general enough to be in `utils.rs` instead of hanging out here.

So pulumi uses a hash of the absolute path as bytes to create a custom workspace dir. What happens if the OS does not encode paths with UTF-8? Would the pulumi tool have to decode, reinterpret as UTF-8, and then re-encode?

(And perhaps the real question: is this anything we're ever going to have to deal with?)
This is more of a cosmetic change, feel free to reject it!

I noticed you pushed an update that allowed you to deal with empty Pulumi configs. Is there any way to write a test for that? (E.g. by creating an empty file masquerading as a config and then running that). Or are there other problems that I haven't forseen?

body: Is there any connection between Pulumi and a rocket? Looking on their site, the default symbol looks pretty close to a cube. I wonder if one of the nerd-font cube symbols might be a better fit.
We can (and I will) write such a test. It will be included with the next commit.
I find the functional style easier to read. I will change it to be explicitly imperative on my next commit.

It's a good point. Pulumi doesn't deal with any encoding, that is handled by Go's [os.Getwd](https://pkg.go.dev/os#Getwd). As far as I can tell, this translates whatever it gets to utf8, but it's platform specific (In Go, a `string` is just `&[u8]`). I don't think we need to care about invalid utf8. 

If it happens, starship will fail to find the stack name, but will otherwise continue. I don't think it's work caring.
